value: Screening and stabilization required regardless of ability to pay
detail: Hospitals with emergency departments that participate in Medicare must provide an appropriate medical screening exam and stabilizing treatment for emergency medical conditions (including active labor) to anyone, regardless of insurance status or ability to pay; payment questions cannot delay screening.
source_name: CMS - Emergency Medical Treatment & Labor Act (EMTALA)

value: Patients at or below 400% FPL eligible for charity care or discount payment policies
detail: California Health and Safety Code 127405 requires each hospital to maintain charity care and discount payment policies; uninsured patients or patients with high medical costs at or below 400% of FPL are eligible to apply; hospitals may not consider the patient's monetary assets in determining eligibility.
notes: Originally enacted via the hospital fair pricing laws; SB 1276 (2013-14) among amending legislation.

detail: California Insurance Code 10123.61 (SB 910, Stats. 2018, ch. 687) prohibits issuing, amending, selling, renewing, or offering short-term limited duration health insurance in California effective January 1, 2019; federal changes to short-term plan rules do not override the state prohibition.
source_name: California Department of Insurance - Notice of Prohibition (SB 910)

value: Not insurance; membership exempts from the California mandate penalty
detail: Health care sharing ministries are not health insurance; membership for at least one day in a month qualifies as a coverage exemption (code F) from California's Individual Shared Responsibility Penalty on Form FTB 3853.
notes: Sharing ministries do not guarantee payment of medical bills.

value: 18-36 months; up to 102% of the full premium
detail: Federal law lets workers and families keep job-based group coverage temporarily after job loss, reduced hours, and other qualifying events; the enrollee usually pays the entire premium plus up to 2%.

value: Age 65+ (or qualifying disability, ESRD, or ALS)
detail: Initial Enrollment Period is the 7 months starting 3 months before the month you turn 65; some people are enrolled automatically from Social Security benefits.
notes: Medicare enrollees are not subject to the Medicaid work requirement.

detail: County welfare offices take Medi-Cal applications and make eligibility determinations; DHCS directs members to keep contact information current and respond to county letters quickly.
notes: Find your county office via the DHCS contact page.

value: County office, Covered California, or the DHCS Help Center
detail: DHCS offers a Help Center, county offices, and Covered California support for applications and questions.
